newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland sells 95 pct of NFI units on primary mkt.
newsitem.headline: Poland sells 95 pct of NFI units on primary mkt.

text.p: About 95 percent of Poles eligible to buy a National Investment Fund (NFI) unit in the country's mass privatisation programme did so, the president of the state-owned bank selling the units said.
"The number of units bought was 25,675,090, nearly 95 percent," Andrzej Topinski, president of bank PKO BP, told a news conference on Monday.
Nearly 28 million adult Poles had one year until last Friday to buy one unit each on the primary market at 20 zlotys.
The units, which have been trading on the Warsaw bourse since July, closed on Monday at 155 zlotys, according to early unofficial figures.

National Securities Depository (KPDW) President Elzbieta Pustola told the news conference that more than 8.5 million units had already been put in book-entry form, a condition necessary for bourse trade.

Deputy treasury minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek, also present, reiterated his ministry's plan to submit issue prospectuses of the 15 NFIs to the Polish Securities Commission (KPW) in the first 10 days of December.
He said the ministry was aiming for the units to be exchangeable into one share in each of the 15 NFIs at the turn of the first and second quarters of next year.
Pustola said that all NFIs would have to be approved for public trade for the units to be exchangeable into shares.

She said that over the 12 months in which Poles could buy the certificate and tranfer it into book-entry form, the number of brokerage accounts in Poland grew by about 10 percent, but it was impossible to know how much stemmed from the NFI scheme.
The 15 NFIs are run by international management firms controlling 512 Polish firms.
Topinski would not say how much his bank earned on its primary market distribution of the certificates, but Kaczmarek said the state budget had gained about 300 million zlotys.
